page: Amazon Web Services c5.18xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8223CL processor with 36 physical cores and 72 virtual cores operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system includes 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25 percent. Memory bandwidth is also strong across both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks. However, single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the average category. Large-model LLM text generation represents a performance tradeoff, with text generation for 135M and 7B models scoring in the bottom 25 percent.

The c5.18xlarge provides a high density of dedicated compute resources relative to its memory footprint. This hardware profile is suited for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from multi-threaded processing, such as database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for local data-intensive storage tasks or heavy deep learning training, but it remains efficient for standard CPU-bound enterprise applications.
